# A build target is named by a value of its own type, not by a string:
# `platform` and `language` are declared in lib/builtin, and each registered
# target carries one const of that type in its own package. PLATFORM and
# LANGUAGE are typed, so a target name cannot be misspelled into a branch that
# is silently never taken.

# The comparison folds, and the branch not taken is removed. This needs a real
# build target, which is why it is here and not a testdata fixture: the
# optimize and parser harnesses register no platforms, so a target's identity
# const does not exist for them to fold.
sngl generate --platform bubbletea --lang go -o out_bt gate.sngl
grep 'always' out_bt/model.go
! grep 'html-only' out_bt/model.go
grep 'go-only' out_bt/model.go

sngl generate --platform html --lang none -o out_html gate.sngl
grep 'html-only' out_html/index.html
! grep 'go-only' out_html/index.html

# A string is not a platform. This is the misspelling the type exists to catch:
# `PLATFORM == "htlm"` was a branch nobody took and nobody was told about.
! sngl check string_compare.sngl
stderr 'operator == not defined for platform and string'

# An unregistered target has no package and so no identity const to name.
! sngl check unknown_target.sngl
stderr 'undefined: htlm'

# A misspelled member of a real target. A package's members are a closed set,
# so this is reported rather than typed dyn -- which is what let every
# misspelled target name compile into a branch nobody took.
! sngl check misspelled_member.sngl
stderr 'undefined: bubbletea.pltform'

# Except where the package says its names are open: html's element set is the
# web's, so `html.marquee` is a tag nobody declared and still resolves -- to
# the wildcard element, which is not a platform.
! sngl check html_wildcard.sngl
stderr 'operator == not defined for platform and element'

# A qualified lookup stops at the last package. It used to walk on into the
# scope every ambient declaration lives in, so `html.color` answered with the
# built-in color type -- and `html.platform` with the built-in platform type
# rather than with html's own identity const, which is how the fold above
# stopped happening.
! sngl check ambient_leak.sngl
stderr 'unknown type "color" in namespace "html"'

-- gate.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:platform/html"
import "sngl:language/go"

window #w(title="t") {
    if PLATFORM == html.platform {
        text(value="html-only")
    }
    if LANGUAGE == go.language {
        text(value="go-only")
    }
    text(value="always")
}

-- string_compare.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

window #w(title="t") {
    if PLATFORM == "html" {
        text(value="x")
    }
}

-- unknown_target.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

window #w(title="t") {
    if PLATFORM == htlm.platform {
        text(value="x")
    }
}

-- misspelled_member.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:platform/bubbletea"

window #w(title="t") {
    if PLATFORM == bubbletea.pltform {
        text(value="x")
    }
}

-- html_wildcard.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:platform/html"

window #w(title="t") {
    if PLATFORM == html.marquee {
        text(value="x")
    }
}

-- ambient_leak.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:platform/html"

window #w(title="t") {
    var c html.color = #ff0000
    text(value="x")
}
